content.text: From Wiktionary, the free dictionary (Received Pronunciation, General American) IPA(key): /ˈpaʊ̯nd/, [ˈpʰaʊ̯nd] Audio (US):Duration: 2 seconds.(file) (Southern US, Midland US, Mid-Atlantic US, New York City, General Australian, New Zealand) IPA(key): /ˈpæʊ̯nd/, [ˈpʰæʊ̯nd] (Pittsburgh, General South African, /aʊ̯/-monophthongization) IPA(key): /ˈpaːnd/, [ˈpʰaːnd] Rhymes: -aʊnd Hyphenation: pound From Middle English pound, from Old English pund (“a pound, weight”), from Proto-West Germanic *pund, from Proto-Germanic *pundą (“pound, weight”), an early borrowing from Latin pondō (“by weight”), ablative form of pondus (“weight”), from Proto-Indo-European *(s)pend- (“to pull, stretch”). Cognate with Dutch pond, German Pfund, Danish pund and Swedish pund. Doublet of funt, pfund, pood, and punt. pound (plural pounds or (UK colloquial) pound) A unit of weight in various measurement systems. quotations ▼ Ellipsis of pound weight. Various non-English units of measure. A unit of mass in various measurement systems. Ellipsis of pound mass. Various non-English units of measure. A unit of mass equal to 16 avoirdupois ounces (= 453.592 g). Today this value is the most common meaning of "pound" as a unit of weight. synonym ▲quotations ▼Synonym: lb A unit of mass equal to 12 troy ounces (≈ 373.242 g). Today, this is a common unit of mass when measuring precious metals, and is little used elsewhere. synonym ▲Synonym: lb t A unit of force in various measurement systems Ellipsis of pound force. Various non-English units of measure. (informal, non-scientific) Ellipsis of pound-force. A unit of currency in various currency systems. The unit of currency used in the United Kingdom and its dependencies. It is divided into 100 pence. quotations ▼ synonyms ▲Synonyms: pound sterling, GBP (symbol), £ (symbol), quid (slang), nicker, sov (slang) Any of various units of currency used in Egypt, Lebanon, Sudan, and Syria, and formerly in the Republic of Ireland, Cyprus, Nigeria, Israel, and South Africa. synonym ▲quotations ▼Synonym: (Ireland) punt Any of various units of currency formerly used in the United States. quotations ▼the Rhode Island pound; the New Hampshire pound (informal) Various non-English units of currency not officially called pounds. quotations ▼ (US) The symbol #. synonyms ▲holonym ▼Synonyms: octothorpe, pound sign; hash, hash sign, hashtag (metonymically); number sign; sharp To be connected, press pound. Internationally, the "pound" has most commonly referred to the UK pound, £, (pound sterling). The other currencies were usually distinguished in some way, e.g., the "Irish pound" or the "punt". In the vicinity of each other country calling its currency the pound among English speakers the local currency would be the "pound", with all others distinguished, e.g., the "British pound", the "Egyptian pound" etc. The general plural of "pound" has usually been "pounds" (at least since Chaucer), but the continuing use of the Old English genitive or neuter "pound" as the plural after numerals (for both currency and weight) is common in some regions. [from 19th c.] quotations ▼ From Middle English pounde, ponde, pund, from Old English *pund (“an enclosure”). Related to Old English pyndan (“to enclose, shut up, dam, impound”). Compare also Old English pynd (“a cistern, lake”). pound (plural pounds) The Village Pound at Wrentham, Suffolk, England A place for the detention of stray or wandering animals. synonym ▲hyponym ▼quotations ▼Synonym: animal shelter (metonymic) The people who work for the pound. quotations ▼ (UK) A place for the detention of automobiles that have been illegally parked, abandoned, etc. synonym, synonyms ▲quotations ▼Synonym: impound Synonyms: (UK) car pound, (US) impound lot, (US) impound A section of a canal between two adjacent locks. synonym ▲Synonym: reach A kind of fishing net, having a large enclosure with a narrow entrance into which fish are directed by wings spreading outward. quotations ▼ (Newfoundland) A division inside a fishing stage where cod is cured in salt brine. synonym ▲Synonym: bulk Manx English uses this word uncountably. dog poundfish poundimpoundLob's poundlobster poundpound puller show ▼±place for the detention of stray animals show ▼±people who work for the pound show ▼±place for detention of automobiles show ▼±section of canal between two locks show ▼±kind of fishing net, having a large enclosure with a narrow entrance show ▼±division inside a fishing stage where cod is cured show ▼Translations to be checked pound (third-person singular simple present pounds, present participle pounding, simple past and past participle pounded) To confine in, or as in, a pound; to impound. quotations ▼ From an alteration of earlier poun, pown, from Middle English pounen, from Old English pūnian (“to pound, beat, bray, bruise, crush”), from Proto-West Germanic *pūn- (“broken pieces, rubble”). Related to Saterland Frisian Pün (“debris, fragments”), West Frisian pún (“debris, rubble”), Dutch puin (“debris, fragments, rubbish”), Low German pun (“fragments”). poun, pown (obsolete or dialectal) pound (third-person singular simple present pounds, present participle pounding, simple past and past participle pounded) (transitive) To strike hard, usually repeatedly. synonyms ▲quotations ▼Synonyms: hammer, pelt; see also Thesaurus:hit (transitive) To crush to pieces; to pulverize. synonyms ▲quotations ▼Synonyms: pulverate, triturate (transitive, slang) To eat or drink very quickly. synonyms ▲quotations ▼Synonyms: bolt, down, chug; see also Thesaurus:eat, Thesaurus:drink You really pounded that beer! (transitive, baseball, slang) To pitch consistently to a certain location. The pitcher has been pounding the outside corner all night. (intransitive, of a body part, generally heart, blood, or head) To beat strongly or throb. quotations ▼As I tiptoed past the sleeping dog, my heart was pounding but I remained silent. My head was pounding. (transitive, vulgar, slang) To penetrate sexually, with vigour. synonyms ▲quotations ▼Synonyms: drill, get up in, nail, poke; see also Thesaurus:copulate with I was pounding her all night! To advance heavily with measured steps. quotations ▼ (engineering) To make a jarring noise, as when running. IPA(key): /puːnd/, /pund/ pound (plural poundes or pounden or pound) A measurement for weight, most notably the Tower pound, merchant's pound or pound avoirdupois, or a weight of said measurement. A pound or other silver coin (including ancient coins), weighing one Tower pound of silver. Money or coinage in general, especially a great amount of it. English: pound Scots: pund, poond “pǒund(e, n.(1).”, in MED Online, Ann Arbor, Mich.: University of Michigan, 2007, retrieved 22 February 2018. Unadapted borrowing from English pound.
